Structural congenital heart disease, most often septal, in a minority of affected individuals. Cardiac involvement is the least penetrant arm of this syndrome and is absent in several well-characterised patients.
One reported patient extends this beyond septation to the left ventricular outflow tract, with a bicuspid aortic valve and aortic root and ascending aortic aneurysm. That is a different morphogenetic field from the atrioventricular cushions the mechanism above runs through, and the mouse literature is explicit that BMP2's role in semilunar valvulogenesis is less well established than its role in the AV cushions. It is curated as part of the cardiac spectrum on the strength of the human observation, not on a mechanism this entry can trace.

nodes.description:
Structural cardiac anomalies, principally septal. Penetrance is clearly incomplete: several well-characterised patients have entirely normal echocardiography, which is what the "with or without cardiac anomalies" clause of the disease name records. No frequency band is given because no cited source supplies a denominator; the defining series reports congenital heart disease as a shared group-level feature of its 12 patients without stating how many had it.
On arrhythmia: the 2025 review lists arrhythmias in the BMP2 haploinsufficiency spectrum, and Wolff-Parkinson-White is curated separately as its own phenotype rather than folded in here. An earlier revision of this entry attributed WPW to the wider 20p13p12 deletion interval and declined to curate it; that was correct on the evidence then cited, and is superseded. PMID:33247540 reports WPW in a patient with an intragenic BMP2 nonsense variant and no deletion, so the neighbouring-gene explanation no longer covers it. Structural and rhythm phenotypes are kept as separate entries because they arise from different developmental steps - cushion transformation for the septal defects, conduction-axis patterning for pre-excitation - and the evidence for each is separate.

nodes.description: BMP2 is not required to build the skeleton once other BMPs are present, but it is required to initiate repair of it. This is the most plausible frame for the phalangeal osteolysis reported in one patient, and it is the reason skeletal surveillance in this disorder is longitudinal rather than a single baseline survey.

Cranial neural crest cells populate the pharyngeal arches and give rise, by intramembranous ossification, to most of the facial skeleton. With less BMP2 they proliferate and differentiate into osteoblasts less well, so the mandible, maxilla and zygoma are built undersized.
On the cell-type binding: CL:0000008 is narrower than this claim. The node concerns osteogenic differentiation of cranial-neural-crest-derived mesenchyme, which is post-migratory, and CL has no post-migratory cranial neural crest term. The migratory term is the closest accurate ancestor of that population, so read the binding as naming the lineage rather than the developmental stage.

nodes.description: In the limb and axial skeleton the sensitive step is osteogenesis from cartilage templates, not chondrocyte differentiation. BMP4 and BMP7 are therefore substantially redundant with BMP2 in the limb, which is the most likely reason the human heterozygote has hypoplastic and dysmorphic bones rather than absent skeletal elements, and the reason this node is annotated for osteogenesis alone.

nodes.description: Tissue-specific homozygous deletion of Bmp2 in cranial neural crest, generated explicitly to model the human Pierre Robin sequence caused by BMP2 haploinsufficiency.
nodes.id: Wnt1-Cre;Bmp2 flox/flox cranial neural crest conditional knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Conditional deletion of Bmp2 in cranial neural crest cells recapitulates Pierre Robin sequence in mice.
evidence.snippet: Mutant mice exhibit severe PRS with a significantly reduced size of craniofacial bones, cleft palate, malformed tongue and micrognathia.

nodes.description: Ventricular preexcitation. This entry previously treated the finding as a neighbouring-gene phenotype of the wider 20p13p12 deletion, which is where it was first described. That reading is no longer tenable on its own: a patient with an intragenic BMP2 nonsense variant and no deletion also has it. One case is not a frequency, but it is enough to stop attributing the finding elsewhere by default.

evidence.reference_title: A de novo pathogenic BMP2 variant-related phenotype with the novel finding of bicuspid aortic valve.

nodes.description: Not a disease model but a variant-function assay: each patient missense allele is tested for its ability to support bmp2b-driven embryonic dorsoventral patterning. Its purpose is allele interpretation, which is why it is linked to the haploinsufficiency node rather than to any phenotype.
nodes.id: Zebrafish bmp2b ventralization assay for patient missense alleles

evidence.reference_title: Monoallelic loss-of-function BMP2 variants result in BMP2-related skeletal dysplasia spectrum.
evidence.snippet: Patient-derived missense variants were modeled in zebrafish to examine their effect on the ability of bmp2b to promote embryonic ventralization.
